assumptions: Capture reagents and multi-omic assays have sufficient sensitivity for low-biomass capture fractions.
Spike-in tracer behaves like endogenous intact EVs for recovery/protection readouts.
Detergent+protease treatment adequately disrupts membranes and exposes protease-sensitive cargo for discrimination.
biological_rationale: If a membrane-protected, capture-positive particle fraction contains a reproducible multi-omic cargo fingerprint across independent production lots, that fingerprint can function as an EV-associated lot-consistency metric independent of a single assigned active molecule.

candidate_quality_attributes.measurement_concept: Presence/absence and detergent-sensitivity of a predefined panel of protected miRNAs and luminal proteins plus lipid-class ratios in capture-positive particle-peak fractions.
candidate_quality_attributes.name: Protected multi-omic cargo fingerprint (miRNA + protein + lipid) in capture-positive particle-peak fractions
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: A composite protected-cargo fingerprint provides a non-numeric lot-consistency metric to distinguish EV-associated cargo from secretome co-isolates.
candidate_quality_attributes.uncertainty: High-to-moderate: requires multi-lot verification and assay sensitivity validation.

edges.competing_explanation: Consistent cargo signals could reflect consistent co-isolation of non-vesicular complexes rather than bona fide EV-protected cargo.
edges.missing_experiment: Protected-cargo profiling on immuno-captured particle-peak fractions with detergent/protease controls and spike-in controls across matched lots.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: guidance supports protected-cargo linkage to EV identity; rodent efficacy shows activity but does not define protected cargo.

edges.competing_explanation: A reproducible analytic fingerprint might not correlate with in vivo delivery or potency; fingerprint reproducibility alone does not establish functional relevance.
edges.missing_experiment: Blinded cross-lot reproducibility testing and subsequent linkage to functional or in vivo short-interval recoverability studies.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate-to-high: establishing a reproducible fingerprint is necessary for CMC gating, but cross-species delivery uncertainties mean functional relevance still requires bridging.

nodes.statement: A membrane-protected, capture-positive particle fraction contains discrete protected cargo elements (miRNAs + luminal proteins) that can be reproducibly detected across production lots.
Detection of a conserved, membrane-protected multi-analyte fingerprint in capture-positive particle-peak fractions distinguishes EV-associated cargo from variable, non-membrane secretome co-isolates.

If the protected-cargo fingerprint is reproducible across >=3 lots, it can be used as a qualitative lot-consistency gate to advance lots for potency linkage and CMC comparability, reducing manufacturing risk from undefined cargo variability.

competing_explanations: Observed conserved cargo could reflect consistent co-isolation of abundant soluble complexes or assay cross-reactivity.
Reproducible fingerprint may not predict in vivo delivery or potency and thus would remain a manufacturing/comparability gate only.
dependencies: analytical platforms for targeted miRNA, proteomics, and lipidomics
validated exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer and capture reagents
design_question: Which intact-EV-associated multi-omic cargo comparison (protected miRNA + detergent-sensitive protein markers + lipid-class distribution) across matched fractionation states best separates lot-conserved EV cargo from variable secretome co-isolates without presuming a single active molecule?
expected_measurable_effect: A qualitative, reproducible presence of a protected multi-omic fingerprint (>=3 protected miRNAs and >=1 detergent-sensitive luminal protein plus consistent lipid-class pattern) in capture-positive particle-peak fractions across >=3 lots; loss of these signals after detergent+protease confirms membrane protection.

experiment.assay: Orthogonal capture workflow with fractionation, particle counts, immuno-capture, detergent+protease protection splits, targeted miRNA, targeted proteomics and lipidomics on capture-positive particle-peak fractions.
experiment.comparator: For each lot, compare capture-positive particle-peak fractions from bounded small-EV fraction versus matched concentrated conditioned-medium fractions; include +/- detergent+protease splits and spike-in controls.
experiment.control: Positive control: characterized small EV preparation processed in parallel; Negative controls: buffer-only and detergent-disrupted samples; spike-in to validate recovery.
dependencies: Analytical sensitivity and platform availability for targeted multi-omic assays
Validated immuno-capture reagents and spike-in tracer performance
Sufficient production lots and material yield
experiment.failure_criterion: No reproducible multi-omic fingerprint across >=3 independent lots, or signals in captured fractions are detergent/protease-insensitive, or spike-in controls reveal assay artifacts.
experiment.falsification_outcome: If falsified, cargo composition cannot be used as a reproducible lot-consistency gate; prioritize alternative attributes (surface-phenotype, spike-in fraction gates), tighten fractionation or source-cell control, or adopt secretome-centric product definitions.
experiment.hypothesis_tested: A reproducible multi-omic cargo fingerprint (protected miRNAs + detergent/protease-sensitive luminal proteins + lipid-class pattern) will be detected in capture-positive particle-peak fractions across >=3 independent lots and lost after detergent+protease.
experiment.primary_readout: Qualitative reproducible presence of predefined protected miRNAs and proteomic markers plus lipid-class pattern in capture-positive particle-peak fractions across >=3 lots and loss after detergent+protease.
experiment.question: Which protected multi-analyte cargo comparison reproducibly distinguishes EV-associated cargo from secretome co-isolates?
required_material: MSC-conditioned medium from >=3 independent production lots (same source-cell bank/passage range)
Matched bounded small-EV fraction and concentrated conditioned-medium outputs per lot
Immuno-capture reagents for intact EV markers (anti-CD63/CD9/CD81 or TIM4/AnxA5)
Particle counter (NTA or TRPS) and reagents
Iodixanol or SEC fractionation materials and fraction collectors
Exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer (orthogonal species or isotope-labeled)
Protease (proteinase K), RNase reagents and detergent (Triton X-100)
Reagents and platforms for targeted small-RNA profiling and targeted proteomics and lipidomics with spike-in/internal standards
Total protein assay reagents and consumables
secondary_readouts: Co-localization metrics (fraction index of particle peak vs capture-positive signal)
experiment.success_criterion: Across >=3 independent lots, capture-positive particle-peak fractions reproducibly show the predefined protected-cargo panel and signals are substantially reduced/abolished after detergent+protease; concentrated secretome controls lack this protected pattern.

explicit_inferences: A protected multi-omic fingerprint that is reproducible across lots can be used as a non-numeric lot-comparability gate.
Spike-in and detergent/protease protection controls are required to distinguish assay failure or co-isolates from true EV-protected cargo.
falsification_criteria: Spike-in controls validate assay recovery but protected-cargo panel members are absent or not detergent/protease-sensitive in capture-positive fractions across >=3 lots.
Detected signals are detergent-insensitive indicating non-membrane association and inability to discriminate EV-protected cargo.
human_decisions_required: Select the predefined protected-cargo panel (exact miRNA and protein targets) and lipid-class metrics to assay
Approve allocation of >=3 pilot lots and resources for multi-omic assays
Decide whether to adopt the fingerprint as a non-numeric comparability gate if reproduced
manufacturability_assessment: Feasible if capture and protected-cargo assays are sufficiently sensitive at intended pilot scale; requires >=3 production lots and validated spike-in controls. Does not assert numeric release limits at this stage.
manufacturing_rationale: A qualitative, non-numeric fingerprint that is reproducible across production lots enables a comparability gate to advance representative lots into bridging and potency-linkage studies without premature numeric release limits.
measurement_strategy: Orthogonal intact-EV capture workflow with density/SEC fractionation to identify particle peaks, immuno-capture of intact material, detergent+protease protection splits, targeted small-RNA panels, targeted proteomics for luminal proteins, and targeted lipidomics on particle-peak fractions; include exogenous spike-in tracer and buffer-compatibility controls.
novelty_statement: This proposal shifts the product-attribute focus from single-molecule potency claims to a composite, membrane-protected multi-omic fingerprint (protected miRNAs + detergent-sensitive proteins + lipid-class pattern) as a non-numeric lot-consistency gate. This is a substantive change from prior hypotheses that emphasized single markers or bulk particle metrics; here the program adopts a composite, protected-cargo fingerprint requiring multi-omic protected-cargo assays and spike-in controls.
principal_risks: Assay sensitivity and compatibility may be insufficient to detect protected cargo in low-biomass capture eluates.
Conserved fingerprints may reflect non-vesicular co-isolates rather than true EV-protected cargo.
A reproducible fingerprint may not translate to in vivo exposure or potency; bridging studies remain necessary.
proposed_potency_relationship: If the protected-cargo fingerprint correlates with a reproducible in vitro protected bioactivity (to be tested), it can be used to prioritize potency-linkage experiments; currently proposed as independent of assumed single active molecule.
proposed_product_change_or_attribute: Define a candidate cargo-consistency fingerprint comprising (A) miRNA species enriched in capture-positive, detergent-protected particle fractions; (B) a panel of detergent/protease-sensitive capture-positive proteins; and (C) a lipid-class distribution that together form a reproducible lot-level signature to gate lot acceptance and prioritize downstream potency linkage studies.
title: Protected multi-analyte cargo fingerprint to distinguish EV-associated vs secretome contributions
